nodes.summary: Resolves git.exe and forwards all arguments to it. git is not on PATH in every shell this repo is used from -- an agent session does not load the user profile that adds it -- and Visual Studio bundles a copy, so this finds it once rather than each caller rediscovering the path. Run with no arguments to get the resolved path on the SUCCESS stream, so "$g = & .\git.ps1" actually captures it; the RetirementCore counterpart uses Write-Host, which goes to the information stream and silently yields nothing. Git's own "-C <path>" forwards correctly (verified), which is how to operate on another repo without changing directory. Targets 5.1 as well as 7, since a shim that resolves a tool is exactly what gets run from whatever shell is open.
caveats: The candidate list leads with this machine's VS 18 Enterprise path. On another machine that misses and the fallback is a recursive Get-ChildItem over the Visual Studio install root, which is slow but only reached once per invocation.

nodes.summary: Concepts to borrow from the MCP code-graph field, tiered by fusion with unique assets. Tier 1: diff-aware test impact (Covers edges backward from git diff), MinHash similarity shortlisting for the prover (makes the section-12 pairwise sweep tractable), measured-coverage import (closes reachable-vs-asserted caveat), graph_diff tool, content-hash incremental indexing + syntax-only fast tier (solves fast per-commit C# nesting). Tier 3 synthesis: plan -> SurgicalEdit -> prover-verify closed loop. Not borrowed: cloud, language breadth, vectors.

Manifest-driven build-and-deploy orchestrator: the generic pipeline (validate-first, git identity stamp, build/package/push gates, stamp-after-push, health poll distinguishing warming from broken, promote hint) lives here; each project declares only nouns in a deploy-manifest.json. Deploy sibling of the manifest-startup pattern.
caveats: Manifest command lines execute as trusted code in the repo root - the manifest is project config, not untrusted input. Only push type azureWebAppZip exists so far; add types in the switch when a new target platform appears. Verify counts only HTTP 200 as healthy. Get-Prop uses the Properties indexer deliberately: .Properties.Name -contains throws under StrictMode when the JSON object is empty.

nodes.summary: Repo-agnostic pre-commit gate: PSScriptAnalyzer, deep nesting (christmas-tree, fail at >=6), Pester, config check, encoding audit. Staged files resolve against git rev-parse --show-toplevel from the CWD, so the one gate serves every repo (the Janet-level decision in note.pre-checkin-style-janet-level). Resolves git via JANET_GIT, then PATH, then the VS-bundled copy - no machine-specific hardcoding.
caveats: Test-Config.ps1 remains absent; that step self-skips.

$LASTEXITCODE is reset before each child-script step: a child that never calls exit leaves the previous child code in place, and the encoding step once failed on the nesting step verdict while printing All clean (caught by the 2026-08-03 smoke test).
C# nesting is not checked per-commit - no fast syntax-only path yet; the C# rule lives in RazorGraph deep_methods / query --deep at repo level.

Module requirements are conditional and fail legibly when unmet: PSScriptAnalyzer only when .ps1 files are staged, Pester 5+ only when *.Tests.ps1 files exist. Both installed CurrentUser 2026-08-03 (PSScriptAnalyzer 1.25.0, Pester 6.0.1); full gate verified green end-to-end on a clean staged file the same day.
